name: Observability
summary: Boot a bounded, agent-managed Grafana + Prometheus + node-exporter stack on your box — an observer seat deploys it, watches it, and explains in plain English how the box is doing, honest about every unknown and failure.

screenshots.alt: A dark Grafana dashboard: System CPU-busy, Memory used (12.2%) and Disk used (5.41%) gauges and a Networking receive/transmit time series — this captured system and network data is node-exporter reading Docker's Linux VM layer on this Mac, not the macOS host; a YC-visitors panel showing 0 local, with YC visitors on the demo VPS; and a Provider auth / rate-limit panel reading UNKNOWN — the stack honest about an unavailable source instead of a fabricated zero

surface.hint: Deploy the bounded metrics stack in your disposable guest, then ask the observer seat how the box is doing

verify: The bounded stack boots in the disposable guest (node obs.mjs deploy — docker compose: Grafana + Prometheus + node-exporter, 127.0.0.1-only, digest-pinned) and Grafana serves the one dark box dashboard

The read-only adapter (box-metrics.mjs) projects the box's visitor + provider JSONL into an owned Prometheus textfile (box_visitor_* / box_provider_*) without modifying the sources, and reports a missing or unavailable source as UNKNOWN (box_*_source_available 0) — never a fabricated healthy zero

Compare the canonical installed source at ~/studio/apps/observability against the box's deployed stack: repair (copy the canonical source in) ONLY if the box stack is missing, provably broken, or provably older than the canonical source; if the box stack is newer (forward drift) leave it untouched and report; if relative age or health is ambiguous, leave it untouched and report to the box lead agent — take no destructive action

verbs.purpose: Prometheus instant query of the box_* and system/network metrics (what the observer seat reads)
Prometheus range query behind the dashboard's time-series panels
Prometheus liveness — is the metrics stack up
node-exporter host metrics (CPU, memory, disk, network) from the guest /proc, /sys, and rootfs
